newsitem.title: GERMANY: Dresdner profit up 40 pct, beats forecasts.
newsitem.headline: Dresdner profit up 40 pct, beats forecasts.

text.p: Dresdner Bank AG on Thursday reported a higher-than-expected rise of more than 40 percent in operating profit last year, outperforming its top domestic rivals in part due to proceeds from dissolving hidden reserves.
Dresdner, Germany's second-largest bank said group operating profit after risk provisions rose to more than 2.8 billion marks from 1.99 billion, according to preliminary data.
It also planned to raise its dividend for 1996 to 1.45 marks from 1.35 marks and pay an additional 10 pfennig per share bonus to commemorate the bank's 125th anniversary.

Dresdner said almost half the increase in operating profit stemmed from earnings on its liquidity portfolio amid gains from the sale of bond holdings in early 1996 as well as proceeds from the sale of share stakes of under five percent.
Dresdner also said it was transferring more than 800 million marks to its reserves.
"Commission income developed very favourably, while both net interest income and ... trading income were also clearly above 1995 results," the bank said in a brief statement.
Provisions for loan losses were only slightly higher than the previous year when they totalled 681 million marks.
The bank did not give a figure for net profit which analysts have forecast to have risen 30 percent to about 1.57 billion marks.
Full results will be reported at a news conference on April 10.
